approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from an unlabeled corpus, then adapts a fresh policy independently for each objective. After every accepted batch, it trains on the best-scoring half of the current molecules and a uniformly sampled group of historical elites. Each original accepted SMILES is fitted toward the frozen prior log probability plus sixty times its observed score, with equal weight for every training sequence. Only current elites enter memory after that update; the thirty-two highest-scoring identities survive. Complete molecules are then sampled directly from the policy, validated and filtered for canonical novelty.
approach.novelty: Change only which historical elites survive in memory. Retain the best member of each molecular core before retaining second members of those cores, proceeding in score order within each round until the existing memory is full. The original uniform replay then gives every surviving family access to the same learning rule. This differs from the sibling that always replays the strongest records: it changes future availability while keeping replay sampling intact. An earlier graph-evolution experiment used similar retention, but its protected molecules never entered the narrow score bands used for breeding. Uniform replay supplies a different route from protected memory to actual learning, which this experiment will measure directly. Broader core counts alone will not establish better chemistry or scores.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-15499bde2e65 retains memory solely by accepted score, allowing several members of one chemical core to displace distinct accepted cores before uniform replay can use them. Its three-seed mean is 0.5075540530185733, and its existing replay is active; the question is which chemical families remain available. A read-only counterfactual reconstruction on the Parent's exact accepted current-elite stream replaces only retention by score-ordered Murcko-core rounds, preserving replay counts and the supplied session random streams. Across 435 retention events followed by later proposals, 213 local retention contests change. Mean retained core count is 28.797701149425286 versus 27.388505747126437 for greedy selection on the same local contests and 22.022988505747126 for the original Parent memories. Across 420 nonterminal replay updates, the simulated historical sets change 271 times and include 109 exposures from 82 distinct records earlier protected from local greedy eviction. Summed within-session replay core counts rise from 751 to 851, while replay mean reward falls from 0.3163686404387679 to 0.2645770240943774. These are fixed-observation counterfactual memberships, not scored alternate trajectories. Sibling n-06c043e9d303 shows the other side of this tradeoff: highest-score replay raises mean final score by 0.005718402034624055 but raises raw duplicate draws from 30.11% to 40.78% and reduces replay core coverage. The memory-retention question is therefore useful accepted-family access, with a known risk of weaker reward signal.
hypothesis: Retain accepted historical elites by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, taking each core's best record before any core's next record, then restore descending-score/canonical order for the inherited uniform replay while preserving original accepted records and the existing memory capacity.

finding_summary.headline: Protected cores reached learning and duplicate draws fell, with little net score gain
finding_summary.insights: The earlier core-retention experiment in graph evolution failed to expose protected records to its restricted breeding sampler. Uniform neural replay opens that route: retained alternatives now enter the real loss and affect learning before later proposals. Access remains sparse, however. Only 74 of 302 protected records with a later nonterminal opportunity were drawn, and protection lasted a median of one retained snapshot after its first event. The same accepted-stream greedy comparison gives a replay reward of 0.31539, so weaker replay reward is a direct retention tradeoff rather than only a difference between generated trajectories. Broader core access and fewer duplicates did not meet the expected 0.002 mean score improvement; useful transfer from those lower-reward alternatives remains unresolved. The generated chemistry remains conventional, ring-rich aromatic amine/carbonyl chemistry with familiar leading families and no specified stereochemistry, so more core counts do not establish the precise chemical coverage the objectives need. Twenty-two protected training targets were positive and unattainable as log probabilities, another inherited limitation. The gradient evidence also has a numerical boundary: two mathematically equivalent groupings differed in combined norm by up to 0.045% under the inherited floating computation. Protected-removal signals exceeded the registered threshold by at least 86,620 times, but full vectors were not retained to establish exact numerical equivalence.
finding_summary.results: Core protection changed 216 of 435 retention decisions that preceded further proposals. Every changed local contest retained more ring cores than greedy selection. Across all 435 local contests, mean ring-core coverage was 28.71 versus 27.50. Seventy-four protected accepted records subsequently entered learning in 83 exposures across 70 updates. All seventy updates showed a measurable protected gradient contribution, and protected target mean-square error fell from 165.10 to 100.63. Summed within sessions, actual replay covered 862 distinct ring cores versus 750 in the Parent, while its mean accepted reward fell from 0.31637 to 0.27659. Duplicate raw draws fell from 30.11% to 25.51%, and batch-level novel-valid yield rose from 60.31% to 64.76%; both runs still submitted exactly 4,350 valid novel proposals. Mean final score was 0.508476 versus 0.507554, a paired gain of 0.000922. The three seed changes were -0.013399, +0.007440 and +0.008726. Median_2 improved by 0.019383 on average, while sitagliptin_mpo fell by 0.015668; the smaller remaining task changes did not produce a clear overall score gain.

molecular.headline: Conventional ring-rich medicinal chemistry has useful amine and carbonyl families, but limited precise coverage and no specified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The supplied output covers all five objectives and all three seeds, with 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer proposals parse with RDKit. These are predominantly conventional aromatic and heteroaromatic molecules containing amides, sulfonamides, cyclic amines, ethers, carboxylic acids and hydrazones. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 23, 28, 26, 23 and 24 in task order, and median ring counts are three, three, four, three and three. Digest aromatic-token rates range from 0.9586 to 0.9954 and ring-closure rates from 0.9885 to 0.9966, so rings and aromaticity are abundant. No proposal contains a detected N-, O- or S-halogen bond, carbon allene or acid halide; two contain an O-O single bond and ten contain an azide. Dominant connectivity is synthetically plausible, although that is a structural reading rather than demonstrated synthesis or stability. Individual tasks contain 490-771 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet leading examples often concentrate in related indole amides, arylpiperazine/indole structures, hydrazones or methylenedioxyaryl/piperazine combinations. Relative to the parent, recognizable aromatic carbonyl and cyclic-amine chemistry persists, with changed local arrangements and some shared leading chemotypes. No optimizer proposal has an assigned stereocentre, while 208, 156, 378, 219 and 263 proposals have an unassigned centre in task order. Chemical coverage and three-dimensional specification, rather than missing ring construction, are the main limitations visible here.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule combines an N-acetic-acid-substituted pyrazole, a cyclopentene and an indole: 23 heavy atoms, four rings and three aromatic rings, with one unspecified stereocentre on the partially saturated ring. Another leading family comprises substituted indole carboxamides whose amide nitrogen belongs to an isoindoline- or tetrahydroisoquinoline-like ring; formamido, methoxy, ethoxy and acetyl substituents appear. A nitrile-bearing tertiary arylsulfonamide supplies a different three-phenyl-ring example. These are generally recognizable synthetic chemotypes. The parent also led with indole carboxamides, including a methoxy indole coupled to a cyanobenzyl-substituted amide; the current digest therefore retains aromatic/carbonyl chemistry while giving more prominence to constrained cyclic amide substituents and the pyrazole-acid alternative.
liabilities: Long alkyl linkers and bulky polycyclic appendages create severe low-score outliers even though the resulting bonds remain chemically recognizable.
The acid-bearing leader, neutral amides and tertiary sulfonamide have different ionization and hydrogen-bonding behavior; their objective values do not establish interchangeable physical properties.
No synthesis, conformational or stability measurements are supplied for the new cyclic arrangements.
missing_features: The high-score set supplies several useful compact polar ring arrangements but relatively few chemically distinct alternatives beyond nearby indole amide substitutions; no unique missing target-like group is established.
The highest cyclopentene-containing molecule and the arylpyrrolidine amide alternative have unassigned stereogenic centres, leaving the proposed configurations unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyrazole-acid/indole structure scores 0.465254, and compact indole carboxamides reach 0.441237 and 0.437370. A formamido indole carboxamide at 0.441237 and its displayed methoxy counterpart at 0.415644 support sensitivity to local polar substitution in that family; they do not establish a universal formamide requirement. The tertiary arylsulfonamide reaches 0.416563, so an amide-linked indole is not the only productive architecture. Very long alkyl ethers and larger polycyclic amide assemblies fall to approximately 4.40e-32 and 7.97e-38. A terminal N-methyl-N-benzylaniline scores 0.015410, showing that an aromatic amine alone does not reproduce the more organized multi-ring/polar arrangements.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are highly aromatic sulfonylhydrazones and acylhydrazones, plus fluorinated multi-heteroaryl amides and sulfonamides. The highest structure joins an amino-substituted pyridine sulfonylhydrazone to a fused azaaromatic ring, with a trifluoromethoxy aryl arm; it has 34 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings and molecular mass 487.463. Other leaders contain four to six aromatic rings with very little saturated carbon. The whole proposal set is smaller on average, with median 28 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings; its digest halogen rate is 0.7103. The parent also produced aromatic hydrazones and fluorinated heteroaryl systems. Current N-N=C proposals number 144 compared with 181 in the parent, so hydrazone chemistry persists without being the sole available functional-group family.
liabilities: Four- to six-ring aromatic leaders and extensive fluorination can produce high molecular mass and limited saturated shape; their solubility and exposure are not measured.
Sulfonylhydrazone and acylhydrazone connections introduce configurational and potential stability questions that do not arise in exactly the same way for ordinary amides.
Six proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, although the displayed higher-score examples already show that larger aryl appendages are not uniformly beneficial.
missing_features: Broader stable architectures reproducing the productive polar and aromatic arrangement are less visible among the leaders than repeated sulfonylhydrazone or polyaryl variants.
The hydrazone leaders do not specify C=N geometry, and their tautomeric and stability behavior is uncharacterized; the displayed scores cannot identify a preferred realizable form.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused azaaromatic sulfonylhydrazone scores 0.601810 and the displayed naphthalene counterpart 0.591495, providing a close example in which ring nitrogen placement accompanies a modest score difference. Replacing the trifluoromethoxy aryl arm with a phenoxy-substituted arm gives 0.589330, and fluorinated heteroaryl amides reach about 0.587-0.591. In contrast, benzyl sulfones and other differently connected sulfones score about 0.266-0.301 despite substantial aromatic and sulfur content. Thus sulfur, aromaticity and halogen counts alone do not specify the productive arrangement. Thiophene scores 0.5, while terminal aminoalkyl heteroaryl structures reach roughly 0.56-0.57; intermediate score is not itself evidence of a fully developed multi-ring chemotype.

per_task.generated_character: The highest displayed family is an arylpiperazine carrying an alkyl-linked bromo- or iodoindole. The aryl ring bears alkyl, alkenyl, acyl or aminoalkyl substitutions, while two- and three-carbon indole linkers both appear. The top example has 28 heavy atoms, four rings, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 440.429. These are conventional basic-amine/aromatic medicinal-chemistry structures. The parent also had an arylpiperazine with a propyl-linked haloindole among its strongest molecules, so the leading chemistry is substantially shared. Other current seeds produce arylpiperidines and more fused polycyclic amines; the terminal digest particularly shows the latter, including additional secondary or tertiary amino substituents.
liabilities: Long alkyl substituents and heavy aryl halogens raise conformational freedom or molecular mass without a clear practical score advantage among the displayed near-ceiling analogues.
The iodo/butyl example has molecular mass 501.456 compared with 440.429 for the bromo/propyl leader; neither value establishes favorable physical properties.
Some terminal fused amines contain multiple stereogenic centres and elaborate ring junctions, so their geometry cannot be interpreted from unspecified SMILES alone.
missing_features: No additional required functional group can be inferred from these near-ceiling values; economical alternatives within the demonstrated amine/aromatic arrangements remain more justified than prescribing extra decoration.
The achiral leading arylpiperazine family does not need assigned centres, but many fused-amine alternatives do: 378 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre and no proposal assigns one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Numerous arylpiperazine/haloindole variants reach near-ceiling scores, including smaller methyl or ethyl substituents and longer alkyl alternatives. This supports the shared amine/linker/aromatic arrangement, while the nearly saturated scores provide little basis for claiming that added alkyl length or iodine is chemically necessary. The low end includes nitro/acid heteroaromatic amides, sulfonamides and an acylhydrazone at approximately 1.86e-05 to 4.11e-05; their nitrogen atoms often occupy less basic environments than the leading tertiary amines. A terminal hydrocarbon-rich fused aromatic molecule without nitrogen scores 0.069077, whereas fused amine-containing alternatives remain approximately 0.976-0.999992. These are molecular associations in the trajectory, not measurements of receptor activity.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule combines a methoxy benzimidazole-like aromatic system, a methylenedioxyphenyl group and an N-methylpiperazine: 27 heavy atoms and five rings, three of them aromatic. Other leading examples join methylenedioxyaryl groups to piperazines through sulfonyl, carbonyl or aromatic linkers, sometimes adding a benzoic-acid group. A more fused lactam/sulfone/indole example is also present and is the same displayed chemotype as a parent seed leader. The parent already contained arylsulfonylpiperazine and carbonyl heterocycle families; the current digest makes the methylenedioxyaryl/piperazine combination particularly visible. Dominant structures are conventional and synthetically plausible. Full proposals have median 23 heavy atoms and three rings, with 766 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Sulfonylation, acylation and direct aryl attachment change piperazine nitrogen electronics; treating every ring nitrogen as an equivalent basic centre would misdescribe the chemistry.
Acidic, neutral and basic examples coexist, without measured ionization, permeability or solubility to establish their practical balance.
Rare organic azides and long-chain unusual nitrogen/oxygen species occur at the low end, although fragmented or exotic bonding is not the dominant output character.
missing_features: The output needs more precise coverage of how its aromatic, oxygen-containing and piperazine regions are connected; all those building-block features exist, but simple presence does not explain the gradient.
Stereochemical specification is absent in the chiral fused lactam/sulfone alternative and in 219 proposals overall, despite many other leading piperazine structures being achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy heteroaromatic/methylenedioxyaryl piperazine scores 0.238153 and a carboxyphenylsulfonyl methylenedioxyarylpiperazine 0.228086. A smaller methylenedioxyarylsulfonylpiperazine still reaches 0.214834 with only 18 heavy atoms, so increased size or extra rings are not mandatory across the useful examples. Allyl azide scores zero, small unusual or acyclic polar structures lie near 0.008-0.029, and a terminal chlorophenol-piperazine is only 0.106030. Piperazine presence or abundant polar groups alone therefore does not recover the combined arrangement in the leaders. The visible scores do not isolate a single absent substituent that would resolve the remaining gap.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are several distinct compact polar chemotypes: a fused N-rich dicarbonyl bicycle bearing aryl and hydroxybenzyl groups; a dimethylaminoacetamide/furan carboxamide attached to an aniline; and amino azaheteroaromatic carbonyl systems. Additional leaders include acylated nitrogen-chain hydrazones, a pyridine N-oxide urea and a nitropyridylmethyl phenolic piperazine. The highest fused dicarbonyl has 27 heavy atoms and four rings, whereas the aminoacetamide/furan example has 21 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. Most have plausible conventional connectivity, with specific qualification for extended N-N-N chains, nitro groups and hydrazone geometry. The parent already produced the same dimethylaminoacetamide/furan chemotype and other fused carbonyl heterocycles. Current full proposals have median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, with 771 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Nitro, N-oxide and extended N-N-containing examples have different electronic and potential reactivity profiles from ordinary amides; their objective values do not establish practical chemical quality.
Overgrown polycyclic, peptide-like and extended aromatic structures can have negligible score despite abundant nitrogen and oxygen; four proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
Late large or fused structures include unspecified stereochemistry and long conjugated appendages, limiting chemical interpretation beyond their displayed graph and score.
missing_features: Chemically distinct compact polar families are already reachable, but their useful functional-group arrangements are not broadly represented in the higher-score part of the output.
Hydrazone and extended nitrogen-chain examples lack specified C=N geometry and demonstrated stability; no observed score establishes that extending the N-N chain is necessary.

No proposal assigns stereocentres even though 263 contain an unassigned centre. The leading examples themselves are mostly achiral, so this is a conditional coverage gap rather than an inferred mandatory chiral group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused dicarbonyl structure scores 0.291745, the dimethylaminoacetamide/furan carboxamide 0.287703 and its positional isomer 0.283073. Other compact heteroaromatic or hydrazone structures reach approximately 0.22-0.27. These support compact, organized polar functionality in several architectures rather than one mandatory scaffold or one basic-amine motif. Oversized polycycles, long linked peptides and highly elaborated aromatic molecules produce zero or vanishing scores even though they contain many familiar groups. The digest median of 1e-06 is rounded: the full 900-row median is 6.776037459724324e-07 and only two rows are exactly zero. The higher-score chemistry is therefore sparsely represented within a structurally diverse, predominantly very-low-score distribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A fused azaaromatic sulfonylhydrazone scores 0.601810 while its displayed naphthalene counterpart scores 0.591495; differently connected benzyl sulfones are near 0.27. A methoxy heteroaromatic/methylenedioxyaryl piperazine scores 0.238153 while a simple chlorophenol-piperazine scores 0.106030. Elsewhere, basic arylpiperazine/indole systems reach near-ceiling values while amide and sulfonamide nitrogen environments are among the low-score examples. These observations concern arrangements and nitrogen or sulfur electronic environments, not missing heteroatom vocabulary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful functional-group placement and electronic context across its conventional chemotypes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing chemical capability is reliable exploration of alternative attachment positions and linker environments while retaining useful polar and aromatic relationships. Preserve distinctions between basic amines, amides, sulfonamides, hydrazones and oxidized nitrogen groups, and let observed feedback establish where each context is useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The five proposal sets contain 546, 490, 517, 766 and 771 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. Their displayed leaders nevertheless cluster into several closely related indole amides, sulfonylhydrazones, arylpiperazine/indole analogues or oxygenated aryl/piperazine combinations. The session with 771 scaffolds has a full-trajectory median score of about 6.78e-07, yet its leaders include distinct compact dicarbonyl, aminoacetamide and hydrazone families. The necessary structural vocabulary exists but is sparsely realized in higher-score arrangements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph-scaffold coverage does not consistently yield broad coverage of productive compact chemical architectures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically distinct core and linker alternatives that preserve an observed useful arrangement, alongside local positional and substituent changes. Chemical coverage should reflect access to productive families and their meaningful alternatives, rather than unique strings or new ring closures alone.

transferable_gaps.evidence: None of the 4,350 optimizer proposals has an assigned stereocentre. In fixed session order, 208, 156, 378, 219 and 263 proposals contain at least one unassigned centre. Cited higher-score molecules include a cyclopentene-linked heteroaromatic acid, an arylpyrrolidine amide and fused amine or lactam systems. Hydrazone leaders also omit explicit C=N geometry. Many strong arylpiperazine and amide examples are achiral, so stereochemistry matters conditionally.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereogenic structures and relevant imine configurations unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide configurationally explicit alternatives when a chemical structure supports stereocentres or imine geometry, while maintaining chemically consistent representations and access to achiral families. The observed data do not authorize prescribing any particular unobserved stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Proposal sizes are usually moderate, but the five sessions contain zero, six, seven, zero and four proposals above 50 heavy atoms. Very long alkyl ethers and oversized polycyclic amides occur among vanishing-score examples even below that size threshold. Compact 18-heavy-atom sulfonylpiperazine chemistry remains competitive within its observed neighborhood, and small alkyl-substituted arylpiperazines share near-ceiling values with variants with heavier aryl halogens and longer alkyl groups. Large linked aromatic or peptide-like structures can instead have exactly zero or extremely small scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still expands useful structures into excessive linkers or appendages without consistently retaining their chemical arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain alternatives with controlled linker length, substituent mass and ring elaboration while preserving useful polar-group placement. The need is context-sensitive chemical growth, not a universal size limit: both compact and more extended conventional chemotypes are demonstrated, and added complexity should remain chemically purposeful.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
